about.bitscribbles: Clear Tracker is made by bitScribbles: small apps, carefully made. Every app starts as a scribble — an idea sketched for a real need — and is refined until it's simple, private and pleasant to use.
about.creditsBody: Built with React, React Router, Dexie and Workbox. Type: Space Grotesk, Inter, JetBrains Mono and Caveat, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. Two sounds are from Mixkit; the other two are made from them. <link>All the licences</link>
about.disclaimerBody: Clear Tracker is a personal tracking tool, not a medical device or treatment program. It doesn't diagnose or treat alcohol use. If you're concerned about your drinking, please reach out to a healthcare professional, or see Resources for help lines in your region.
about.free: Clear Tracker is free, with no ads and no paid version. If it's useful to you and you'd like to support bitScribbles, you can <coffee>buy me a coffee ☕</coffee>.
about.notBackupOwn: Browser storage isn't a backup. Clearing your browser's website data erases it, and Safari can delete a site's data after seven days without a visit — unless the app is added to your {{place}}, which keeps its own record. Back up from time to time.
about.notBackupShared: Browser storage isn't a backup. Clearing your browser's website data erases it, and the browser may clear it if the device runs very low on space — less likely once installed. Back up from time to time.
about.notInstalled: Not installed — open in a browser tab
about.p1: A record, not a score. Nothing you log undoes anything. A drinking day counts as much as a clear one.
about.p2: Your aim, your call. Cutting back and stepping away completely are both valid. You set the intention, and can change it any time.
about.p3: Private by design. No account and no cloud: everything stays on this device unless you back it up.
about.p4: Calm, not clinical. Plain words, no warnings or rebukes, and no streak that punishes a choice you made.
about.p5: Made for everyone. Works with screen readers and keyboards, in light, dark and high contrast, and respects reduced motion.
about.persistUnknown: Persistent storage: unknown in this browser
about.storedBody: Everything you log — clear days, drinking days, and your intention history — is stored only in this browser, on this device. There's no account, no cloud sync, and nothing is ever sent anywhere unless you back up yourself from Settings.
about.supportBody: Help lines and programmes for your region are on <resources>Resources</resources>, and answers to common questions on <help>Help</help>.

onboarding.aiming_one: Aiming for {{count}} clear day a week. Every day you log adds to the picture — there's no score to keep.
onboarding.aiming_other: Aiming for {{count}} clear days a week. Every day you log adds to the picture — there's no score to keep.
onboarding.alreadyIos: Already added Clear Tracker to your Home Screen? Open it from there — this browser tab keeps its own, separate record. Can't spot the icon? Swipe down from the middle of the Home Screen and search for “Clear Tracker”.
onboarding.alreadyMac: Already added Clear Tracker to your Dock? Open it from there — Safari keeps its own, separate record. Can't spot it? Search for “Clear Tracker” with Spotlight (⌘ Space).
onboarding.howBody: On Check-in, tap a day to select it, then tap it again to log it. Each tap moves it on a level, and back to not logged. Try it on this practice day — it isn't saved.
onboarding.howNote: Days you don't log are simply not logged — nothing assumes how they went. Past days can be logged or changed at any time.
onboarding.intentionBody: How many clear days would you like to aim for each week? You can change this any time.
onboarding.laterOwnRecord: You can still install later, but your days won't move across by themselves — you'd back up here and restore it there.
onboarding.laterShared: You can install later from the browser menu; your days come with you.
onboarding.oneDevice: Each phone or computer keeps its own record, so use Clear Tracker on one device.
onboarding.practiceLabel: Practice day: {{level}}. Tap for the next level.
onboarding.practiceTry: Tap the day to try it
onboarding.privacyBackUp: Back up now and then. Settings can make an encrypted backup, protected by a passphrase you choose, to keep wherever you like. Check-in reminds you after 30 days.
onboarding.privacyNoAccount: No account, no cloud. Nothing you log is sent to bitScribbles or anyone else, and there are no ads.
onboarding.privacyOnlyHere: Only here. Your days are stored on this device{{where}}. Clearing its website data, or losing the device, loses them.
onboarding.privacyTitle: Your record stays on this device
onboarding.soundsAndroid: They play at your media volume.
onboarding.soundsIos: On iPhone, they follow the silent switch.
onboarding.soundsSub: A tone for each level when you log a day.
onboarding.supportBody: Resources lists help lines and programmes for {{region}}, including someone to talk to any time. Help answers common questions about the app.
onboarding.supportWhere: Both are linked from the bottom of Check-in, and in Settings.
onboarding.thenOpen: Then open it from your {{place}} and carry on there.
onboarding.welcomeBody: A simple way to track days you choose not to drink — whether that's cutting back or stepping away completely. There's no wrong way to use this.
onboarding.whatItIsBody: A private record of your days, and how they add up over weeks and months.
onboarding.whatItIsntBody: A medical service or treatment programme. It doesn't diagnose, advise or judge. If you're concerned about your drinking, a healthcare professional can help.
onboarding.whyClearBody: A clear day is a day without alcohol. The name means a little more: a clearer head, and a choice that’s yours.

trends.emptyBody: Once you've logged a few days, this is where patterns show up — which days tend to be clear, how your weeks line up with your intention, and how much you've tracked.
trends.estFoot: From logged days, counting A few as 1.5 drinks, Moderate as 3.5 and A lot as 5 — its minimum, so a period with an A lot day could be higher.
trends.estIntro: Rough figures from the levels you logged — for context, alongside your clear days.
trends.gridKey: Each tile is a week, showing its clear days. "2 of 4": weeks met that month. "Not enough logged": short of the intention, but with days not logged that could still make it — log them to settle it.
